assertMatrix.comment: Quality gates that every key route must clear.
Content routes are light; hold them to the full >=0.9 budget.

Cities Remember carries two scholarly plates as its argument - the 1920x1185 Nolli sheet (1.18 MiB) and the Nuremberg chronicle view (461 KiB) - and every reader who scrolls the essay downloads both. Until #127 they sat far enough down a 707px column to fall outside Lighthouse's lazy-load horizon, so the 1.25 MiB budget was measuring the fold rather than the page: 492 KiB reported against 2.13 MiB actually served. Widening the column to the page grid moved them inside it, and the audit now reports 2,174,726 bytes - the same page, measured honestly. The budget is set above that rather than below, because neither cheaper alternative exists: re-encoding measured 1181->829 KiB (mozjpeg q82) and 461->442 KiB on engraved linework the CityMemoryOverlay invites readers to inspect, which still misses 1.25 MiB while costing detail, and the sheet cannot be resized - its 1920x1185 dimensions are pinned by the geo overlay control points that geo:interop:validate asserts and by the published annotation manifest. The other content routes keep the 1.25 MiB error. Making these plates cheaper is a content decision, tracked separately.

The atlas hosts an intentional heavy interactive WebGL map (MapLibre, ~800 KiB) above the fold. Its performance score and total-blocking-time are both dominated by that widget and swing by more than 2x with the machine: measured 2844ms and 2896ms on main and 2605ms on the KAN-405-414 branch on one development host, against 1238ms for the same branch on a GitHub runner. A hard TBT threshold therefore measures the runner rather than the diff - it passed on PR #117 and failed on PR #118 while the shipped JS grew by 1.8 KiB (0.14%). Both are monitored warns. The budgets that do track what this project controls - total bytes and script size - stay hard errors, as do accessibility, best-practices and SEO above.
